corrected_finding.finding: Missing owner policies made the copied cursor dictionary smaller than the fixed requested A/B notification domain. The actual native027 binding rejects unequal key sets; the synthetic Session originally omitted this requirement.
corrected_finding.resolution: The new private extraction sets exactly A/B cursors. The original due and activate expressions still iterate only present policies. Inverse AST now restores both the cursor assignment and final aggregate. The four owner-domain synthetic cases now enforce native cursor-key equality.

read_scope: Complete new branch and synthetic test source, with the corrected extraction reread.
Original native-domain branch notification span, assess_cell and capture_partial.
Owner-local dispatch and retained historical policy source; original local executed expression.
Native027 archived notification binding owner/cursor key checks.
conclusions: The incumbent index is derived uniquely from the declared historical incumbent action, not assumed to be index zero.
Each start_owner uses its own actual dispatch result and ledger; differing peer proposals do not block policy creation. Missing owners remain explicit and have no fabricated policy.
The two reversible continuation edits affect the cursor domain and final aggregate only; original notification, tick, retry, admission and due-policy order remain.
The retrospective composite uses A initial/return and B supply/later components only in post-run assessment. It is not sent to a policy or predictor.

The original physical assessor still requires actual transfer ACKs, executed edges, same-tray lifecycle, all five jobs and mandatory Storage. A prediction or local guard is not presented as actual protection.
Partial capture keeps actual client/session evidence and uses const diagnostics without result_at after failure.
The branch keeps strict_protected unknown and complete-request100ms false; new whole prospective evidence is still required.
limits: Source-only review: no imports, tests, model predictions, native runs or runtime source-closure verification.
The 21 synthetic cases were read, not independently collected or executed.
A future saved verifier must bind the new initial record schema and actual branch envelope; the old fixed-vector initial verifier cannot be reused unchanged.
Exceptions may terminate the experimental branch with partial unknown evidence; this review does not claim distributed failure recovery.
